L01.text: The Leaning Tower of Pisa started tipping over when it was only two or three floors tall.

L02.text: Pisa, eleven seventy-three. A heavy marble bell tower, on soft clay and sand, with a foundation only about three meters deep.

L03.text: Within a few years, one side was sinking.

L04.text: Then Pisa went to war with its neighbours, and building stopped for almost a hundred years.

L05.text: Which, by accident, saved it. The soil had time to settle and firm up.

L06.text: When the builders came back, they made the new floors taller on the short side. So the tower curves, like a banana.

L07.text: The bells went on top in thirteen seventy-two. And it kept on leaning.

L08.text: By nineteen ninety, it leaned about five and a half degrees, and they closed it.

L09.text: Engineers stacked hundreds of tonnes of lead on the high side, then gently drilled soil out from underneath.

L10.text: Luckily, it worked. The top came back about forty centimeters. Unluckily, it's still leaning. On purpose, this time.

L11.text: Tourists still line up to hold it up. Technically, they're not helping.
